timeline.what: Four university students were killed inside the King Road rental house in Moscow, Idaho, while two housemates slept there.
A surviving housemate reported seeing a masked man in black walk past her and out of the house.
A white Hyundai Elantra was recorded circling King Road and passing the house at least three times.
The white Hyundai Elantra sped away shortly after the murders were believed to have occurred.
A 911 call reported an unconscious person; police arrived and found no murder weapon and no sign of forced entry.
Investigators found a tan leather knife sheath with Marine Corps insignia and a single sample of male DNA on its button snap.
Fear emptied the campus as students left Moscow while police said they had no suspect, weapon, or explanation.
Kohberger bought a military-style knife and sheath online.
Police matched the white Hyundai Elantra to Kohberger and used DNA from rubbish outside his parents' home to link him to the sheath DNA.
FBI agents and state troopers raided the family home in the Pocono Mountains and arrested Kohberger.
Kohberger was flown back to Idaho and charged with four counts of first-degree murder.
The King Road house was demolished.
The case was moved to a Boise courtroom, with trial set for summer 2025.
Bryan Kohberger pleaded guilty to all four murders as the prosecution agreed to remove the death penalty.
A judge sentenced Kohberger to four consecutive life sentences without parole plus ten years for burglary.
